body.cap: Inthetech conducts interviews with media representatives from five countries—the United States, France, the United Arab Emirates, Taiwan, and Vietnam—during the Global Media Meetup | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Inthetech Co., Ltd. (CEO Seung Ho Choun) announced that it participated in the “Global Media Meetup” hosted by AVING News’ International Press Club (IPC) for domestic companies and startups on Friday, the 12th at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul.

The Global Media Meetup focuses on introducing Korean companies’ and startups’ products and technologies to the global market. In particular, it aims to proactively report on CES 2026 Innovation Award winners and CES-participating startups through global media channels and expand business opportunities.

Inthetech is a global healthtech company that develops digital healthcare and AI-based solutions to improve cognitive function. The company provides a digital therapeutics and training platform that simultaneously addresses treatment and prevention for users experiencing cognitive decline and attention-related issues, including dementia, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and ADHD.

Its flagship solutions include the digital cognitive rehabilitation solution EYAS, the mental training and learning platform COGPLAY, and the AI-based digital therapeutics solution EYAS FOCUS, which won a CES 2026 Innovation Award.

Inthetech emphasized that its technology is designed with scalability to cover more than 5.5 million actual users undergoing cognitive management and training worldwide, as well as a potential prevention population exceeding 600 million people. The company aims to address structural issues, including aging, mental health challenges, and declining attention, in the global digital health market.

body.cap: Inthetech CEO Seung Ho Choun speaks during an interview with overseas media representatives. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Inthetech currently exports its products to 12 countries and continues to achieve strong business performance, particularly in Asian markets such as India, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, and Australia, centered on medical institutions, educational organizations, and healthcare partners.

In India, the company is establishing a joint venture with a local partner to pursue long-term localization and large-scale market expansion. By obtaining CE MDR certification, Inthetech is also on the verge of entering European digital health markets, including Germany, France, and the United Kingdom, with commercial rollout imminent.

The company is preparing for U.S. FDA approval with a target of 2026 and plans to fully enter the U.S. digital therapeutics and healthcare market following approval. In parallel, Inthetech plans to establish overseas offices in London and Silicon Valley starting in 2026 and is expanding its global footprint to support partnerships, investment attraction, and technology collaboration.

EYAS FOCUS, which received the CES 2026 Innovation Award in the Digital Health category, is an AI-based predictive digital therapeutics solution that earned high scores across all evaluation criteria, including technological excellence, aesthetics, innovation, and global problem-solving capability.

EYAS FOCUS uses AI algorithms to analyze users’ cognitive behavior data, response patterns, and changes in attention levels in real time. This enables precise early-stage prediction of ADHD and cognitive decline, personalized training and treatment pathway design, and long-term management and improvement of mental function.

body.cap: Inthetech Team Lead Heejae Lucy Lee presents during the Global Media Meetup. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: From an aesthetic perspective, the solution employs intuitive UI/UX and game-based interactive design, making it easy for users of any age, culture, or level of digital familiarity to use. This design significantly improves treatment continuity and user engagement.

EYAS FOCUS also gained recognition for its innovation by presenting a next-generation predictive digital therapeutics model that simultaneously delivers treatment and prevention, clearly differentiating it from conventional digital therapeutics approaches.

Its global problem-solving potential also drew attention. Amid worldwide challenges such as aging populations, mental health issues, and disparities in access to healthcare, EYAS FOCUS offers a scalable digital alternative that can expand to more than 600 million people in the potential prevention population and over 5.5 million individuals requiring active management.

Inthetech stated, “After introducing our products to the global market through CES 2025, receiving the CES 2026 Innovation Award for EYAS FOCUS has validated both our technological capability and market potential,” adding, “We expect this achievement to become a turning point for full-scale global business expansion, including increased global media exposure, more meetings with buyers and medical and healthcare companies, and heightened interest from investors in the digital health and DTx sectors.”

Meanwhile, AVING News has introduced Korean companies to the world through partnership cooperation with more than 800 media outlets across 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building on its long-established global media network, AVING News launched the International Press Club in August. Media outlets participating in this Global Media Meetup included Innovation & Tech Today from the United States, Le Café Du Geek from France, Arageek from the United Arab Emirates, and Digitimes from Taiwan.
